stem: During long-term post-transplant care coordination, which monitoring responsibility should the coordinator emphasize at routine follow-up visits?

options.text: Obtain laboratory tests and studies to monitor immunosuppression levels and organ function
Discontinue all laboratory monitoring after the first clinic visit
Monitor only the recipient's vacation plans without clinical data
Rely exclusively on patient self-report without any objective studies

explanation.rationale_correct: Health maintenance after transplantation includes obtaining all laboratory tests and other studies to monitor levels of immunosuppression and organ function.

rationale_incorrect.B: Long-term follow-up requires ongoing laboratory and clinical monitoring rather than discontinuation after one visit.
rationale_incorrect.C: Clinical monitoring of immunosuppression and organ function is required beyond nonclinical topics.
rationale_incorrect.D: Objective laboratory and study data supplement patient self-report in post-transplant coordination.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → g. Health maintenance → i.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Obtain all labs tests and other studies to monitor levels of immunosuppression and organ function

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → g. Health maintenance after transplantation → i. (monitor immunosuppression levels and organ function); PDF p. 117 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fifth 030500 item; general lab-monitoring coordination distinct from clinic intervals (cctc-3014/3024) and community MD communication (cctc-3015); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.

stem: When planning discharge antimicrobial prophylaxis for a solid-organ recipient, which infection prevention measure may be included based on patient-specific risk?

options.text: Medications to prevent Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) when indicated
Permanent discontinuation of all antimicrobials for every recipient
Prophylaxis based only on the recipient's preferred brand of toothpaste
Routine live-virus vaccines at discharge for all immunosuppressed recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Antimicrobial prophylaxis decisions are patient-specific; anti-bacterial and anti-fungal medications may be given to prevent Pneumocystis pneumonia, thrush, and other infections of concern.

rationale_incorrect.B: Many recipients receive indicated antimicrobial prophylaxis rather than universal discontinuation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Prophylaxis is based on donor- and recipient-specific infection risk, not personal product preferences.
rationale_incorrect.D: Live-virus vaccines are contraindicated after transplantation; discharge planning uses indicated antimicrobial agents instead.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → medication management → v.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: medications may be given to prevent Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP), thrush, and other infections

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → medication management → v. (anti-bacterial/anti-fungal prophylaxis including PCP prevention); PDF p. 107 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fifth 030600 item; PCP prophylaxis angle distinct from CMV (cctc-3023), grapefruit interaction (cctc-3031), and missed-dose teaching (cctc-3014); anchor verified on Cupples p. 107.

stem: A coordinator is updating long-term malignancy-prevention teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Recipients should reduce malignancy risk through recommended screening and a healthy lifestyle.
Continuing smokers should be counseled about increased lung cancer risk.
Immunosuppression eliminates all post-transplant cancer risk without screening.
Smoking cessation resources should be offered to recipients who continue to smoke.

explanation.rationale_correct: Long-term teaching includes recommended malignancy screening, healthy lifestyle, counseling continuing smokers about lung cancer risk, and offering smoking cessation resources. Immunosuppression increases rather than eliminates cancer risk.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also correct—smoking cessation resources should be provided.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement III is false; immunosuppression increases malignancy risk and screening remains important.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false; not all four statements are correct.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → g. Health maintenance → iii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Reduce risk of malignancy through recommended screening … Counsel recipients who continue to smoke about the increased risk of lung cancer; provide smoking cessation resources

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → g. Health maintenance after transplantation → iii. (malignancy screening, smoking counseling, cessation resources); PDF p. 117 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Synthesized item. Eighth complex_combo in bank; distinct from late-mortality combo (cctc-3020) and post-transplant diabetes (cctc-3028); anchor verified on Cupples p. 117.

stem: A recipient on cyclosporine reports bothersome excess hair growth and asks whether another calcineurin inhibitor might have fewer cosmetic effects. Which counseling point is MOST accurate?

options.text: Tacrolimus is less likely to cause cosmetic problems such as hirsutism than cyclosporine
Cyclosporine never causes cosmetic side effects
All calcineurin inhibitors guarantee identical cosmetic side-effect profiles
Cosmetic effects require immediate graft removal without medication review

explanation.rationale_correct: References note tacrolimus is less likely to result in hyperlipidemia and cosmetic problems than cyclosporine, which is associated with effects such as hirsutism and gingival hypertrophy.

rationale_incorrect.B: Cyclosporine is specifically associated with cosmetic adverse effects including hirsutism.
rationale_incorrect.C: CNI agents differ in cosmetic side-effect profiles rather than being identical.
rationale_incorrect.D: Cosmetic CNI effects are managed through medication review and team guidance, not automatic graft removal.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Tacrolimus is less likely to result in hyperlipidemia and cosmetic problems than cyclosporine
